title: MZ Scale game window via script call?

posts.author: CT_Zeal
posts.body:
Hi! I was wondering if anybody's made a plugin for RPG Maker MZ where you can change the scale of the game window via a script call and/or a button press.
There's a script for VX Ace called
Fullscreen++ by Zeus81
and I essentially want that functionality for RPG Maker MZ. With Fullscreen++ you can press F6 to scale the screen from 544x416 to 1088x832, exactly doubling the resolution. And if you have a larger display you can scale it up again, allowing you to scale the game until it hits your monitor borders essentially. There's also a button for pressing F5 to go into windowed borderless mode, and you can still scale the game window in fullscreen which is great for people who prefer pixel-perfect resolutions.
I also want this functionality to be able to be called via a script call, since I have a custom options menu with a window scale setting in it.
To be clear, I don't want this to simply increase the game's resolution. I have a custom resolution and I just want the window to appear 2x, 3x etc. larger but stay the same internal resolution when adjusting the setting.

I don't think it has been updated so you can open up the console/devtools during your playtest by pressing f8 or f12 (sometimes f10 depending on if you have other plugins that change it) and type in slowly (it will populate the info for you like a search bar) something like this:
JavaScript:
$dataSystem.advanced.screenScale
When you get to the screenScale part, type it in slowly to see what it suggests and go with that. Change the value to whatever you need (1, 2, or 3).
That being said, there might even be a $gameSystem part of it that saves it to memory so you can try searching through the game system's corescripts (in rmmz objects) for it.
I don't have MZ and it looks like you might have the latest version which I don't have access to so it may or may not be in there.
Hope this helps!

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Great! It's very possible I've missed something, but if so then (naturally) I can't see what it is.
The
outerWidth
stuff is to account for the window's title bar and borders, which are typically larger on top/bottom than left/right. But I only use that for deciding on the scale in
addScaleMultiplier
, so I don't think that's it.
If you're on a multi-monitor setup then yes, there might be various reasons for this kind of thing. (I have no real experience with multiple monitors, so this is just guesswork.) Test with the game window on each monitor, if you haven't already, to see if there's a difference. Otherwise maybe the NWJS
moveBy
method and/or OS screen settings are getting quirky. E.g. if the window is near the edge of the current screen, and is told to move partially onto the other screen, perhaps its position is capped to the current screen.
Someone more knowledgable might happen along with more concrete answers~
